transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: 54 minutes | Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Nina Valdez (Redwood CSM) — Olivia Park, Mark Torres, Priya Singh, Ethan Li, Grace Nwosu (BlueAnchor)

[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Avery from Redwood, i'm the account lead here, and with me are Samir our solutions engineer and Nina our customer success manager. how's everyone's afternoon?
[00:09] Olivia Park: good, thanks. appreciate you making time. we wanted this to be a quick orientation — we've got legal loops and security queued but wanted to align before we start provisioning.
[00:20] Mark Torres: yeah i got a calendar invite, and i pulled the staging network details. we'll share after. sorry if my audio is a little crunchy.
[00:28] Samir Rao: no worries mark. quick agenda: overview of onboarding runway, security checklist (vpc, kms, sso), pilot scope (dedicated capacity), and then ops / runbook handoff. we'll leave 10 minutes for q&a.
[00:40] Priya Singh: great. i mostly want to confirm encryption key flow — we have strict KMS usage and HSM-backed keys for PII processing. do you guys support customer-managed keys for private deployments?
[00:50] Avery Chen: yes, for Redwood Private and Dedicated with private control plane we integrate with customer KMS — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS and HSM flows. the docs we'll send include the KMS key policy example and how to configure key rotation.
[00:59] Ethan Li: is that available for Hosted API as well or just private?
[01:03] Samir Rao: hosted has envelope encryption but customer-managed keys are available on Dedicated/Private tiers only due to isolation and compliance. small note — sometimes our catalogue page shows CMK as "bring-your-own-key" which gets shortened in the docs.
[01:17] Grace Nwosu: and audit logs? we need 12 months of immutable audit trail, show of admin changes and token usage for SOC2.
[01:25] Nina Valdez: we can enable longer retention on the Console — for Enterprise customers we have add-on retention. we also emit audit logs to your cloud logging endpoints and can ship to S3/GCS for long-term archival.
[01:38] Olivia Park: good. on the networking side we prefer VPC peering to minimize egress. can you speak to peering versus private-link? also are there any extra networking costs?
[01:48] Samir Rao: sure — we support VPC peering and provider-specific private-link equivalents. peering is the quicker path in most clouds; private-link gives tighter control but sometimes costs more. our default recommendation is peering for staging + private-link for prod if you need extra isolation. regarding costs we can share rough egress estimates; but if you run Dedicated in same cloud region the intra-region egress is typically cheaper.
[02:13] Mark Torres: sounds fine. we'll try peering in staging first. i'll drop the CIDR blocks after the call.
[02:19] Avery Chen: perfect. pilot scope — from our side we recommend a 2-week pilot on a small Dedicated pool (2x A100-ish equivalent) to validate latency SLOs and cost curves with your real prompt set. Samir, could you run through the benchmark plan?
[02:31] Samir Rao: yeah — plan is: 1) get sample prompt set from Olivia (top 10 real-world prompts), 2) run baseline on Hosted (for comparison), 3) run on Dedicated with batching/kv-cache enabled, 4) gather latency percentiles and per-token cost and present a short results doc. we'll also do a streaming test and function calling scenario.
[02:58] Olivia Park: quick clarification — when you say KV cache, are we talking about prefix caching or the token-level kv? we've got long user sessions so preserving KV for reuse matters.
[03:08] Samir Rao: good call — Redwood runtime supports both prefix caching and KV cache reuse for conversation flows. we'll set cache TTLs and explain tradeoffs: longer TTL reduces per-token cost but may increase memory footprint. sometimes our docs abbreviate KV cache to "KV cash" — ignore that, it's a transcription quirk.
[03:26] Priya Singh: haha, yeah i saw that in an earlier doc. on data residency — all inference logs and telemetry for this pilot must reside in our EU region. can you ensure region pinning?
[03:38] Avery Chen: absolutely. we can pin Dedicated pools to eu-west-1 and route requests via region specific endpoints. Console will reflect token-level cost and latency per region.
[03:47] Mark Torres: what about model variants — if we need to fallback to a quantized variant during capacity spikes, how is that handled?
[03:55] Samir Rao: the platform has automated fallback policies — you can set routing by latency or cost. if Dedicated saturates we can fall back to a compatible quantized model on hosted with single-tenant routing to reduce cold starts. we'll show you the rollout policy config in the runbook.
[04:12] Ethan Li: will there be any SDK changes? our app uses the node sdk and has some custom retry logic.
[04:18] Nina Valdez: SDKs are backwards compatible for typical generation endpoints. for streaming or function-calling you might adopt a small change — we can provide a compatibility snippet. Samir will paste code samples in the follow-up.
[04:30] Olivia Park: ok, on stakeholders — our legal wants the SOC2 + contract addendum, security wants the KMS/HSM flow, and infra needs the peering setup. timeline wise we want pilot to start by 2028-03-20 and a decision within 4 weeks after pilot. is that doable?
[04:46] Avery Chen: yes that timeline is tight but doable. we'll prioritize the security pack and the benchmark scheduling.
[04:52] Grace Nwosu: about SSO: do you support SAML and SCIM for user management in Console? we need SAML SSO and automated group provisioning.
[04:59] Samir Rao: yes SAML and SCIM are supported; we can also support OIDC if you prefer. we'll send the metadata XML and SCIM endpoint details.
[05:08] Priya Singh: quick question on encryption in-transit: are connections strictly TLS1.3? we have some older infra that only does 1.2 but we'd prefer 1.3.
[05:16] Avery Chen: we default to TLS1.3 for clients, but support 1.2 as needed for compatibility. for Dedicated/private we'll ensure TLS1.3 for production.
[05:25] Olivia Park: any gotchas around rate-limiting? we might have bursts tied to batch jobs.
[05:31] Samir Rao: Console exposes per-route quotas and token throttling. For Dedicated you get higher throughput and you can configure burst lanes. We also support graceful queuing with SLA tiers so you don't get hard rejects during spikes.
[05:46] Mark Torres: great. what's the on-call/incident process? who do we ring if latency doubles in the middle of the night?
[05:53] Nina Valdez: you'll have a dedicated CSM and access to our Escalations page — enterprise support includes 24/7 on-call for Sev1s. we'll provide a runbook and contact rota.
[06:04] Olivia Park: cool. can we walk through a short runbook sketch?
[06:09] Samir Rao: quick sketch: 1) alert triggers (latency p95 >X), 2) automatic mitigation (scale-up Dedicated pool or route to fallback), 3) notify via PagerDuty + Slack channel, 4) CSM/SE engaged and post-mortem. We'll share a editable runbook.
[06:27] Ethan Li: i also wanted to check embedding/semantic search — we have a vector index in Pinecone. can Redwood generate embeddings and push to Pinecone, or do we need a separate job?
[06:36] Samir Rao: you can use Redwood to generate embeddings via the embeddings endpoint and then post-process to Pinecone. we also have a connector pattern that our integration team can help wire, but for the pilot simplest is to run a small batch job from your infra that hits our embeddings endpoint and writes to Pinecone.
[06:51] Priya Singh: are there any known compliance certifications beyond SOC2, like ISO 27001?
[06:55] Avery Chen: we have SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 in progress in some regions, and we can provide a compliance pack. Specifics depend on the deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
[07:06] Grace Nwosu: you mentioned telemetry — how granular is token-level cost reporting? can we tag requests by microservice or customer?
[07:15] Nina Valdez: yes you can attach token-level metadata and tags. Console shows cost broken down by route, model, and tag. We'll include tagging examples in the docs.
[07:25] Olivia Park: ok next, procurement — our procurement team wants an estimate for pilot and potential monthly cost for a small Dedicated pool. could you provide a ballpark?
[07:33] Avery Chen: we can; we'll include a sample cost model in the follow-up. It's usually presented as a per-token estimate plus a reserved capacity baseline for Dedicated. Samir will give the numbers in the benchmark doc.
[07:46] Mark Torres: any firewall rules? we have strict egress polices; what's the minimal set of endpoints to allow?
[07:53] Samir Rao: we'll send a short list — control plane endpoints, region-specific inference endpoints, and logging endpoints for audit stream. We'll also include CIDR ranges for peering.
[08:03] Olivia Park: team, any blockers on our side?
[08:07] Mark Torres: none immediate — i'll get CIDRs and a staging account provisioned.
[08:11] Priya Singh: just need the KMS policy example to review with our crypto team.
[08:16] Ethan Li: i'll collate our top-10 prompts and expected SLAs (p50/p95 goals) and email by Friday.
[08:24] Avery Chen: perfect. i'll recap after the call and send the security pack and the benchmark plan. Samir, Nina — anything to add?
[08:33] Nina Valdez: i'll set up the pilot workspace in the Console and share access once Mark gives staging creds.
[08:40] Samir Rao: i'll draft the benchmark steps and include the code snippets for node + python.
[08:45] Olivia Park: ok we're at 35 minutes in, any final q's?
[08:50] Grace Nwosu: curious about escalation SLA for Dedicated — is there an uptime SLA written into the reserved contract?
[08:57] Avery Chen: yes for Dedicated we have SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. those are part of the reserved capacity contract; legal will include the exact numbers in the addendum.
[09:07] Priya Singh: also confirm retention TTL for logs — you said add-on can handle 12 months, what's the default?
[09:14] Nina Valdez: default is 90 days. we'll add the 12 month retention option in the follow up.
[09:21] Olivia Park: great. recap of next steps?
[09:24] Avery Chen: recap: 1) send SOC2/KMS docs (Avery) by 2028-03-09, 2) Samir to deliver benchmark plan and sample Prompts template by 2028-03-12, 3) BlueAnchor to share staging CIDRs and prompts by 2028-03-13, 4) schedule dedicated deep-dive 60m session for week of 2028-03-14, 5) pilot to start 2028-03-20.
[09:46] Olivia Park: that aligns with our internal timeline. thanks everyone.
[09:50] Avery Chen: thanks all. we'll follow up with notes and links: SOC pack, runbook template, and the benchmark spreadsheet. bye!

AUTO-GENERATED ACTION ITEMS (end of transcript)
- Avery Chen: Send SOC2 and KMS integration pack (includes KMS policy examples, HSM notes, and rotation guidance).
- Samir Rao: Create benchmark plan with p50/p95 latency targets, cost calc and sample prompt harness.
- Nina Valdez: Provision pilot workspace and invite BlueAnchor users to Console.
- Mark Torres: Share staging VPC peering details and create a staging keypair for access.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache), speaker overlap a few times, some proper nouns may be slightly off.

References mentioned: onboarding runbook (link: https://redwood.example/runbooks/onboarding), SOC2 pack (link: https://redwood.example/security/soc2-pack), benchmark template (link: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/template)
